page: Amazon Web Services c6gn.8xlarge is a compute-optimized server instance powered by custom AWS Graviton processors. Built on the 64-bit ARM64 architecture, this instance features 32 dedicated physical cores running at 2.5 GHz with a Neoverse-N1 microarchitecture. It provides 64.0 GB of system memory, yielding a compute-focused ratio of 2.0 GB per core. The instance operates on the AWS Nitro hypervisor and includes a high-speed networking interface delivering 50 Gbps of baseline bandwidth, though it lacks local NVMe storage and integrated GPU hardware.

Performance benchmarks place this instance in the middle tier for multi-core compute and memory throughput. The 32 physical cores achieve a stress-ng multi-core score of 48,563.42 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 11,689.0, reflecting solid parallel processing capabilities. Memory bandwidth is notable, reaching 1,894.04 GB/sec for cached small-block reads and 181.11 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads. However, single-core performance is a relative tradeoff, with a Geekbench single-core score of 973.0 and a weak rating in single-threaded gzip compression.

From a workload perspective, the c6gn.8xlarge is highly suited for network-intensive and compute-bound applications. It demonstrates strong capabilities in static web serving at 33.08 GB/sec and handles database operations efficiently, as evidenced by a Redis SET throughput of 38.79 million operations per second. The ARM64 architecture offers qualitative cost efficiency by delivering high multi-core density and 50 Gbps networking at a lower resource-to-cost ratio compared to traditional x86 alternatives, making it an optimal fit for distributed microservices, software compilation, and multi-threaded data processing.

Operating at 2.5 GHz, it features 64.0 GB of system memory, providing 2.0 GB per core, and delivers a baseline network bandwidth of 50 Gbps without local storage or GPU accelerators. Benchmark data indicates average multi-core performance, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 11,689.0 and a stress-ng multi-core score of 48,563.42, alongside strong memory read bandwidth of up to 1,894.04 GB/sec. Single-core performance represents a tradeoff, scoring lower in single-threaded compression tests. Qualitatively, the ARM-based architecture offers high resource density and cost-efficient compute power.
